q-175701.name: Question 1
q-175701.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $6$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y-6 & =10 \\ -2y-6+6 & =10+6 \\ -2y+0 & =16 \\ -2y & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y & =16 \\ \frac{-2y}{-2} & =\frac{16}{-2} \\ \frac{\cancel{-2}y}{\cancel{-2}} & =-8 \\ y & =-8\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: −8

q-175701.html:
Question 1
?
If −2y−6=10, then y=
−8
.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the addition principle, adding 6 to both sides: −2y−6=10−2y−6+6=10+6−2y+0=16−2y=16

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by −2: −2y=16−2y−2=16−2−2y−2=−8y=−8
q-175701.knowledge_point: Solving Linear Equations that Involve Multiplication

q-177723.name: Question 2
q-177723.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $9$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+9 & =7 \\ -x+9-9 & =7-9 \\ -x+0 & =-2 \\ -x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle. We multiply by $-1$ to get rid of the negative sign.

$$
\begin{aligned}-x & =-2 \\ (-1)\cdot (-x) & =(-1)\cdot (-2) \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?
If −x+9=7, then x=
2

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting 9 from both sides: −x+9=7−x+9−9=7−9−x+0=−2−x=−2

Second, we apply the multiplication principle. We multiply by −1 to get rid of the negative sign. −x=−2(−1)⋅(−x)=(−1)⋅(−2)x=2
q-177723.knowledge_point: Solving Linear Equations that Involve Multiplication

q-58208.name: Question 3
q-58208.worked_solution:
To save time, we will keep the variable on the right-hand side as we solve. First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $1$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}16 & =3y+1 \\ 16-1 & =3y+1-1 \\ 15 & =3y+0 \\ 15 & =3y\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}15 & =3y \\ \frac{15}{3} & =\frac{3y}{3} \\ 5 & =\frac{\cancel{3}y}{\cancel{3}} \\ 5 & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Since $5=y,$ we conclude that the solution is $y=5.$

q-58208.html:
Question 3
?

Solve for y where 16=3y+1.

a
y=4
b
y=112
c
y=5
d
y=92
e
y=3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To save time, we will keep the variable on the right-hand side as we solve. First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting 1 from both sides:

16=3y+116−1=3y+1−115=3y+015=3y

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by 3:

15=3y153=3y35=3y35=y

Since 5=y, we conclude that the solution is y=5.

q-175704.name: Question 4
q-175704.worked_solution:
To save time, we will keep the variable on the right-hand side as we solve. First, we rewrite the right-hand side by placing the term containing the variable first:

$$
\begin{aligned}23 & =3+5x \\ 23 & =5x+3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $3$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}23 & =5x+3 \\ 23-3 & =5x+3-3 \\ 20 & =5x+0 \\ 20 & =5x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}20 & =5x \\ \frac{20}{5} & =\frac{5x}{5} \\ 4 & =\frac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} \\ 4 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $4=x,$ we conclude that the solution is $x=4.$

q-177743.name: Question 5
q-177743.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $5$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{7}x-5 & =-4 \\ \frac{1}{7}x-5+5 & =-4+5 \\ \frac{1}{7}x+0 & =1 \\ \frac{1}{7}x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, multiplying both sides by $7:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{7}x & =1 \\ \cancel{7}\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{7}}x & =7\cdot 1 \\ x & =7\end{aligned}
$$

q-175711.name: Question 6
q-175711.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $3$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}x-3 & =7 \\ \frac{1}{2}x-3+3 & =7+3 \\ \frac{1}{2}x+0 & =10 \\ \frac{1}{2}x & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, multiplying both sides by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}x & =10 \\ \cancel{2}\cdot \frac{1}{\cancel{2}}x & =2\cdot 10 \\ x & =20\end{aligned}
$$

q-2540.name: Question 7
q-2540.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $2$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{5}+2 & =\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{x}{5}+2-2 & =\frac{2}{3}-2 \\ \frac{x}{5}+0 & =\frac{2}{3}-\frac{6}{3} \\ \frac{x}{5} & =-\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, multiplying both sides of the equation by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{5} & =-\frac{4}{3} \\ \cancel{5}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{5}} & =5\cdot (-\frac{4}{3}) \\ x & =-\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

q-175715.name: Question 8
q-175715.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $3$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}-3 & =-\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{x}{2}-3+3 & =-\frac{1}{3}+3 \\ \frac{x}{2}+0 & =-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{9}{3} \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, multiplying both sides of the equation by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & =\frac{8}{3} \\ \cancel{2}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{2}} & =2\cdot \frac{8}{3} \\ x & =\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
